night_26_27.Japan: No islandwide banzai. About 75-120 infiltrators/local counterattack personnel probe seams and support nodes. One remaining Type 95 may make a short local move but is not committed to a mass tank charge.
night_26_27.effect: The temporary seaward diversion of some US destroyer attention helps one infiltration penetrate a support/communications locality, but US illumination, artillery, M4A2 and machine-gun defenses contain it by dawn.

dawn_state.US_behavior: Treat every surviving pocket as a reduction problem: tank/engineer/75-mm teams with observed naval/CVE fires. No broad unsupported infantry rush; damage assessment remains imperfect.

day_progress: Morning: US re-establishes full close-fire coordination after the night surface alarm and reduces western/central residual positions; Japanese local wires/ammunition keep several pockets dangerous even after islandwide C2 has failed.

Midday-afternoon: Green Beach logistics and verified lanes permit sustained engineer explosives, flamethrower/demolition work, ammunition and evacuation. Japanese mobile armored capability effectively expires as the last Type 95 is destroyed, immobilized or cut off.

Late day: US controls most useful maneuver/logistics terrain, but eastern/northern strongpoints and several isolated bombproof clusters still require organized reduction. Tarawa is not declared secure at T24.

T24_state.territorial_assessment: US controls roughly the great majority of Betio and all useful bulk landing/logistics nodes; coherent Japanese resistance remains in multiple strongpoints, so this is still organized reduction rather than pure mop-up.
T24_state.secure_gate: Do not declare secure on 27 Nov. Centered final organized collapse now remains a 28-Nov evening to 29-Nov morning problem, to be generated from the 27T24 state rather than copied.
